messages:
Elyse: thinking we should ship a small 'contingency policy editor' in Console so teams can compose automatic fallback rules (triggers -> contingency action -> audit). want quick UX feedback on what knobs are essential

Raj: +1. main concern: surface area. teams will want per-route overrides and pin-to-model-version. i suggest a simple builder UI with presets + an 'advanced YAML' toggle for power users :thinking_face:

Sam: must include a live 'simulate' or dry-run. users should be able to run the policy against recent traffic (last N minutes) and get estimated fallback counts and examples. otherwise it's scary to flip on

Mike: from design perspective: three-pane builder works best: left = triggers, middle = action, right = audit/telemetry. triggers: dropdowns for error types (5xx, timeout, latency_p90/p95, quality_regression), thresholds, and logical composition (AND/OR). action: contingency modes: route->variant, return->cache, return->static-response, queue/retry. audit: sampling rate + full-trace vs metadata + retention slider

Elyse: on audit defaults: i propose 100% full trace for SLO-impacting fallbacks and 1% for capacity-based fallbacks. need to balance cost and compliance needs

Raj: suggestion: two audit levels: 'full-trace' (input + output + kv + headers) and 'metadata-only'. retention and KMS scope configurable per-policy. default mapping: safety/quality -> full-trace; capacity/latency -> metadata-only

Sam: also: immutable policy change log. every create/update should append an audit entry with who changed what, timestamp, and before/after. must be easily queriable and downloadable as CSV/JSON

Mike: UX detail: after user selects triggers show an 'expected impact' card: estimated fallback rate (based on recent traffic) + small sparkline. include a 'simulate' button to run examples. avoid forcing users into another page for simulation

Elyse: workflow idea: create global policy -> attach to routes -> optionally pin to region/model-version -> set canary percentage. support both global and per-route policies

Raj: triggers: allow presets like 'latency degradation', 'model-timeout', 'safety regression' for non-technical PMs. advanced users can build boolean expressions: e.g. `latency_p95 > 800ms AND error_rate > 1%`

Sam: operational requirement (backend): every fallback event must emit a telemetry envelope: fields = route, model_variant, trigger_type, contingency_action, policy_id, policy_version, request_id, timestamp. this is critical for alerting and dashboards

Mike: copy note: maybe call 'degrade mode' -> 'contingency action' to be less negative in PM comms. allow teams to set a friendly display name for a policy

Elyse: audit UI idea: table with filters (policy_id, route, trigger_type, time window) + per-row expand showing side-by-side original model output vs fallback output; include redaction toggle for full traces and a link to download event package

Raj: everything in Console must be backed by an API: CRUD + simulate + audit-list. ensure RBAC: modify permissions separate from view-full-traces permission

Sam: retention defaults: 30 days for full-trace, 365 for metadata. legal will want longer for some customers; show cost estimate in UI and allow per-customer override

Mike: next steps for design: I'll mock the three-pane builder, simulate modal, and the audit table. will include inline YAML editor and small help tooltips

Elyse: action items: Raj - draft API contract + event schema + simulate endpoint. Sam - retention/quotas and telemetry storage model. Mike - wireframes. I'll sync w/legal on retention defaults
